title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant

£30,000-£35,000 Full-Time Permanent Cambridge

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Assistant Accountant to join a growing finance team in a varied and hands-on role.

Working closely with senior finance leadership, you'll play a key role in supporting month-end processes, maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring the smooth running of day-to-day finance operations.

This position would suit someone with previous finance experience who is looking to broaden their responsibilities and gain further exposure to management accounting and financial reporting.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting with the preparation of monthly management accounts.
- Maintaining purchase and sales ledgers.
- Performing balance sheet and ledger reconciliations.
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving queries.
- Supporting payment runs and cash management activities.
- Managing company credit card and expense reconciliations.
- Preparing VAT returns and ensuring compliance with deadlines.
- Assisting with budgeting, forecasting and year-end processes.
- Producing financial reports and analysis as required.

About You
- Previous experience within an accounts or finance role.
- Strong understanding of double-entry bookkeeping.
- Experience with reconciliations and month-end activities.
- Good Excel skills.
- Experience using accounting software.
- Studying AAT or actively developing an accounting career would be advantageous.
- Organised, proactive and keen to learn.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £30,000-£35,000.
- Full-time permanent position.
- Monday to Friday working pattern.
- Supportive team environment with opportunities for development.
- Exposure to a broad range of finance responsibilities.
- Pension scheme and generous holiday entitlement.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an Accounts Assistant or Assistant Accountant looking to take the next step in their career and gain wider exposure within a well-rounded finance function.

For more information, please apply or get in touch for a confidential discussion.

- Experience managing customer accounts and collecting outstanding debt.
- Strong customer relationship and communication skills.
- Experience working with SAP or another ERP system would be advantageous.

- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
- The ability to investigate and resolve account queries and disputes effectively.
- Excellent organisation and time-management skills.
- The ability to manage your own workload and prioritise competing deadlines.
- Resilience and confidence working towards financial KPIs and collection targets.
- A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively with sales, customer service and finance colleagues.

Salary & Benefits

£35,000-£38,000 + excellent benefits, including:

How to Apply

If you're an experienced Credit Controller or Accounts Receivable professional who is fluent in Italian and English and looking for an international role with excellent hybrid flexibility, we'd love to hear from you.

Jonathan Grimes

The Language Business

title: Credit Controller
description:
Robert Half are delighted to be partnering with an established and highly regarded business based in Cambourne, Cambridge, to recruit a Credit Controller to join their finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys taking ownership of their ledger, building strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders, and playing a key role in improving cash collection and reducing outstanding debt.

Reporting into the Credit Control Manager, you will take responsibility for a designated portfolio of customers, working closely with operational teams across the business to ensure debts are managed effectively and queries are resolved promptly. The role offers a varied workload within a supportive and collaborative finance environment.

Responsibilities

As the Credit Controller, you will be responsible for:
- Managing and monitoring the collection of outstanding customer balances
- Working towards monthly cash collection targets
- Building effective relationships with customers and internal stakeholders
- Preparing and distributing aged debt reports
- Issuing customer statements and collection correspondence
- Managing accounts that require credit restrictions or "on stop" procedures
- Investigating and resolving queries that may be delaying payment
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date customer account records
- Processing daily cash receipts, allocations and monthly direct debit payments
- Supporting the setup of new customer accounts
- Supporting the Credit Control Manager with projects aimed at improving cash collection and overall credit control processes

Your Profile

- Previous experience working within Credit Control
- A proven track record of successfully collecting debt and delivering against targets
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise a busy workload
- Good knowledge of Excel
- Previous experience using ERP/accounting systems, with IFS experience advantageous
- A proactive, professional and positive approach
- The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a wider team
- A full UK driving licence

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary of £30 - £32,000
- Hybrid working (Three days in the office and two from home)
- Opportunity to join an established business
- Varied Credit Control position, with plenty of interaction across the wider organisation.
- Occasional travel to other locations across the UK.

title: Town Planner
description:
Job Title: Town Planner

Location: Cambridge

Penguin Recruitment is delighted to be supporting a leading planning consultancy with the appointment of an experienced Town Planner to join their growing team in Cambridge.

This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated planning professional to work on a varied portfolio of projects, providing planning advice to clients across a range of development proposals. You will work within a collaborative and supportive team, with excellent opportunities for continued professional development and long-term career progression.

The Role

As a Town Planner, you will be involved in a broad range of planning projects, working closely with clients, local authorities, consultants and other stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Preparing planning appraisals for land, buildings and development proposals.
- Undertaking planning policy research, site assessments and analysis.
- Preparing and submitting pre-application enquiries, planning applications and appeals.
- Drafting planning statements and other supporting documentation.
- Contributing to Design and Access Statements, Sustainability Statements and associated reports.
- Managing a varied portfolio of projects and ensuring work is delivered within agreed timescales.
- Liaising and negotiating with local planning authorities, consultees and other stakeholders.
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with clients and industry contacts.
- Attending and presenting at client meetings, public consultations, Parish Council meetings and Planning Committees where required.
- Developing practical and commercially focused planning strategies.
- Preparing high-quality reports and providing clear planning recommendations.
- Keeping up to date with planning legislation, policy, guidance and wider market trends.

About You

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- MRTPI qualification or be working towards chartership with significant relevant experience.
- Previous experience within a planning consultancy, local authority or similar planning environment.
- Strong knowledge of the UK planning system, planning policy and development management.
- Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
- Commercial awareness and confidence dealing directly with clients.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and planning research tools.
- A full UK driving licence and willingness to travel when required.

Candidates with transferable skills and relevant experience are encouraged to apply. The client is open to considering individuals who may not meet every requirement but can demonstrate strong potential and a genuine interest in developing their planning career.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary dependent on experience.
- 25 days' annual leave, increasing to 28 days after three years.
- Life assurance of four times basic salary.
- Private medical cover and health cash plan following probation.
- Travel insurance following probation.
- Salary sacrifice pension scheme.
- Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave.
- Holiday buy-back scheme.
- Long service awards.
- One paid volunteering day each year.
- Smart working policy to support a healthy work/life balance.
- Full-time position of 37.5 hours per week.
- Part-time working arrangements considered.
- Ongoing training and professional development.
- Excellent long-term career progression opportunities.

title: Purchasing Assistant
description:
Purchasing Assistant

Initially a 3 month contract with the possibility of moving into a maternity cover.

Hybrid Working Available

Are you looking to build a career in purchasing and procurement?

We are working with a well-established organisation that is looking to appoint a Junior Purchasing professional to join its procurement team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who has either recently started their career in purchasing or has gained some initial exposure to procurement activity and is now looking to develop their skills further.

You don't need to have extensive purchasing experience. Perhaps you have been involved in raising purchase orders, obtaining quotations, communicating with suppliers or supporting an existing procurement team and are keen to take the next step.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and external suppliers, you will help ensure goods and services are purchased efficiently, competitively and in line with business requirements.

What will you be doing
- Raising and processing purchase orders accurately.
- Requesting and comparing supplier quotations.
- Liaising with suppliers regarding orders, deliveries and queries.
- Supporting supplier research and purchasing decisions.
- Following up on outstanding orders and resolving issues.
- Maintaining accurate purchasing records and supporting internal stakeholders.

What are we looking for?

This role would suit someone who is early in their purchasing or procurement career and is keen to develop.

You may already have:
- Some experience within purchasing, procurement, buying or supply chain.
- Experience raising purchase orders or processing orders.
- Exposure to communicating with suppliers and requesting quotations.
- An understanding of basic purchasing processes.
- Strong attention to detail and good organisational skills.
- The confidence to communicate with both suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- A proactive approach and willingness to learn.

We would also consider candidates from a purchasing administration, sales administration, customer service or supply chain support background where there has been some exposure to suppliers, orders or purchasing activity.

A CIPS qualification or studying towards one would be advantageous, but is not essential.

The opportunity

This is a great opportunity to join an established procurement function and gain broader exposure to purchasing, supplier management, sourcing and procurement processes.

For the right person, the role offers the opportunity to develop commercially and professionally while building a long-term career within procurement.

If you have some initial purchasing experience and are looking for your next step, we'd be keen to hear from you.

title: Medical Receptionist / Administrator
description: Abbeyview Surgery is a GP Surgery in rural Lincolnshire serving circa 9300 patients. We have a diverse, friendly team that work hard to provide the best quality care to our Practice population. Providing front of house support to patients and various administrative support to our team of clinicians, as needed from time to time. this will include some administrative duties outside of reception duties. Experience within a reception/administrative position is essential. Job summary Medical Receptionist Duties:- Greet patients and visitors in a professional and friendly manner- Answer phone calls and direct them to the appropriate department or individual- Schedule appointments and manage the appointment calendar- Check-in patients- Maintain patient records and update information as necessary- Handle incoming and outgoing emails- Ensure the waiting area is clean and organized Main duties of the job Skills:- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills- Strong organisational and multitasking abilities- Attention to detail and accuracy in data entry- Proficiency in using office equipment such as computers, printers and scanners- Ability to maintain patient confidentiality Overview of your organisation If you are a motivated individual with excellent customer service skills, we would love to hear from you. This is a great opportunity to join a dynamic team in a fast-paced medical practice.
